references.text: The preceding verse describes the condition where leprosy breaks out and covers the skin, leading to the priest's assessment in verse 13.
A similar statement that the priest shall declare the sick person clean when the plague has turned white, with the same conclusion: 'he is clean'.
Describes the cleansing ritual for a leper after the priest has declared them clean, following up on the declaration in 13:13.
Miriam is struck with leprosy that is 'white as snow', and Moses prays for her healing - illustrating leprosy and cleansing.
Naaman was cleansed of leprosy, but Gehazi was afflicted with leprosy 'white as snow' - a contrast between cleansing and judgment.
Jesus heals a leper and commands him to show himself to the priest as a testimony, in accordance with the Mosaic Law on cleansing.
Jesus heals ten lepers and sends them to the priests to be declared clean, according to the regulations in Leviticus.
